project.name: Nook
project.description: Nook is a community platform for the 1337 / 42 student community. This monorepo contains the Next.js client, User, Chat, and Game services, Code Arena and its judge worker, databases, object storage, gateway, and monitoring. The current playable game supports authenticated 1v1 and 2v2 programming matches.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with Nook’s product overview: a community platform for 1337 and 42 students that brings profiles, friendships, a feed, conversations, and games into one app. It introduces Code Arena as the current playable game, with authenticated 1v1 and 2v2 programming matches. This map sets up the client, service, data, and infrastructure stops ahead.

tour.title: Client Experience
tour.description: From that product map, start at the browser shell: the root layout provides application metadata, global styles, fonts, and shared providers. The client guide maps routes, workspaces, and data flows, showing where profiles, chat, and Play appear in the experience.

tour.title: Browser Integration
tour.description: Building on the client shell, the integration guide traces browser APIs, Socket.IO, and signed MinIO paths through Nginx. The Chat client handles conversations, feed, attachments, and read states, while the Arena transport sends match commands and adapts authoritative snapshots. Together they show how browser actions reach backend services.

tour.title: Service Topology
tour.description: The Compose guide explains startup, environment ownership, networking, storage, and routing for local operation. Compose connects the HTTPS gateway and Next.js client with the User and Chat backends, giving you the deployment map before you examine service responsibilities.

tour.title: Identity and Profiles
tour.description: With the service boundaries in view, the User service owns authentication, recovery, OAuth, profile images, and social features. Its Prisma schema records identity, friendship, block, and authentication relationships, while AccountsService implements profile lookup, search, updates, deletion, and image storage. This shared identity model supports Nook’s other services.

tour.title: Chat and Feed
tour.description: Chat owns conversations, groups, messages, realtime events, attachments, and game notices, while the feed reuses a public Chat group and client APIs. Its Prisma schema models the conversation and message data, and the GameChallenge record connects an Arena room and match ID to the conversation carrying the challenge. This shows how social features extend the identity and browser flows from earlier steps.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma models describe database entities and relations; ordered SQL migrations evolve the persisted schema over time.

tour.title: Code Arena Engine
tour.description: The Code Arena specification defines 1v1 and 2v2 behavior, scoring, privacy, and service contracts. The shared engine owns authoritative actions and round transitions, while the Game service coordinates matchmaking, private rooms, and lifecycle events; Records describes the match data shape. Compose connects the Game backend to storage, the judge worker, User service, and RabbitMQ.

tour.title: Shared Match Experience
tour.description: Building on the authoritative match flow, ArenaWorkspace brings the editor, problem, tests, score reveal, and sidecars together for players. The socket transport adapts server snapshots and sends commands, the Yjs client synchronizes shared source and peer cursors, and the team-chat client handles message and ping history. These pieces form the browser experience for collaborative matches.

tour.title: Isolated Code Judging
tour.description: The game engine’s judge contract describes execution requests and results, and the worker starts a bounded queue with image-readiness checks. Its container image packages the worker and Docker CLI; Compose gives it the Docker socket on a private judge network and connects the Game service to that worker. This boundary keeps untrusted submissions in the dedicated judging path.

tour.title: Durable Data
tour.description: The shared persistence contract separates match, submission, reveal, collaboration, and evaluation-claim storage from gameplay, while its PostgreSQL adapter implements transactions for those records and account erasure. Compose provisions a dedicated Game database for match and submission records. Chat’s GameChallenge table keeps the room-to-conversation link used by the invitation flow.

tour.title: Project Verification
tour.description: Finish with the verification guide’s repeatable checks, disposable integration-service boundaries, and security controls. The GitHub workflow runs the project gate on pull requests, main-branch pushes, and manual dispatch, including the repository check command. The lifecycle test demonstrates that coverage at the game level by exercising a complete three-round 1v1 through scoring and reveal.
